result.summary: Round-2 re-validation of lib/letflow/design/iss0923-catalog-delete-blocks-on-pinned-instances.md, read-only (no lib/test edits, no mutants, no mix run needed; git status shows only the unrelated untracked letflow-3.code-workspace). Every rework-1 fix re-derived from real code. (1) Section 6 race mechanism VERIFIED: Engine.create/2 (engine.ex:450-461) -> start_instance/6 (engine.ex:532-589) runs PinResolver.resolve(graph, definition, pin_lookup(attrs, prefix), ...) BEFORE create_snapshot (engine.ex:1318, SnapshotStore.create opens its own Repo.transaction, snapshot_store.ex:119) and before persist/14 (engine.ex:1506, one Multi committed by Repo.transaction at :1661); pin_lookup/2 (engine.ex:1278-1281) defaults to PinLookup.build(); PinLookup.catalog_lookup/1 (pin_lookup.ex:63-73) is a plain `Repo.get(Entry, service_id)` returning {:error, :not_found} for nil AND for status :RETIRED; moduledoc :16-20 says START-time lookup. create/2 itself is not wrapped in a transaction, so a FOR SHARE in catalog_lookup would release at statement end: the claim that a lock needs an engine-level transaction (wrap R..P or lock inside persist's Multi) is correct, as is the conclusion that a delete/1-only FOR UPDATE is useless against a plain SELECT. Both interleavings (create-before-delete -> pinned instance on deleted service; delete-before-create -> rejected at start, no snapshot/projection because R precedes S) and the 'guard 3 only sees an instance once BOTH snapshot and projection are committed' claim match the code (guard 3 is an inner join). Retire-first reasoning matches (RETIRED -> :not_found at start; resolve_pinned_version still resolves existing pins per ISS-0917). (2) Ordering/sort fix VERIFIED: TenantProvisioning.list_registrations/0 is `Repo.all(Registration)` with no ORDER BY (tenant_provisioning.ex:274-276); design now normatively removes tenant-order dependence (no early exit, per-tenant LIMIT cap+1, concatenate, global ascending sort, take cap, truncated iff combined > cap). I checked the logic: the globally smallest cap ids are always inside each tenant's smallest cap+1, and combined>cap iff total>cap (a single tenant contributes cap+1, otherwise sum equals total). UUID ordering in Postgres (byte order) equals lowercase-hex text order. (3) AC-6/8/11 refs VERIFIED: service_catalog_test.exs describe 'AC6' at :376, test :377, delete assertion :384-385, success tests :392 and :400, concurrent-delete test :427 (to ~:453); :461-471 is describe 'AC7: update_scope/2', correctly excluded. (4) AC-8 seam VERIFIED against migrations: instance_definition_snapshots.definition_id REFERENCES process_definitions(id) on_delete :nothing, null: false (20260816193002_create_instance_definition_snapshots.exs:93-100, constraint name instance_definition_snapshots_definition_id_fkey); definition_name/definition_ver/graph null: false, snapshotted_at default now() (:102-106); instance_projections.definition_id (20260818110001:71) is `add :definition_id, :binary_id, null: false` with NO references clause, so one shared process_definitions row is the only FK prerequisite; tenant_id was dropped from projections (20260820000003); remaining projection columns default (current_nodes, variables, join_counters) or are nullable. (5) req373 doc item VERIFIED: req373-service-catalog-version-lifecycle.md:352-353 lists delete/1's three outcomes and :359-361 accepts orphaned archive rows; req192-service-catalog-routes.md:446 holds the delete->409 mapping row; iss0917 design has the OQ-3 row (:156 mentions OQ-3). The 'unique index lives on service_catalog_versions, Entry only has unique_constraint' wording fix matches migration 20260921000004:91-93. Rest of design re-checked and still holds: every ISS-0923 requirement (decide block vs document; MINOR) maps to D-A..D-L and AC-1..AC-14; signatures, error shape (instance_refs() map with exactly instance_ids/truncated), router clause (handle_delete case at admin_services.ex:275-287 has no catch-all, so the clause is mandatory), Error constructor sibling at error.ex:428-437, cross-module deps (TenantProvisioning, InstanceProjection.terminal?/1 true only for :completed/:cancelled, InstanceDefinitionSnapshot, Entry, Version, Api.Error, Routers.AdminServices) all listed; no TBD/deferral language (OQ-1/OQ-2 carry defaults); no implementation code (prose data-flow only). Security reasoning INV-1/2/5/6/7/8 sound.
issues: MINOR (design section 10.2 AC-8 seam, non-blocking): the sentence 'other columns default or nullable' for the instance_projections direct insert is not fully accurate: timestamps(inserted_at: :started_at) gives started_at and updated_at as NOT NULL with NO DB default (20260816120003:45-47 via timestamps(), schema instance_projection.ex:163). Repo.insert!/2 on the schema struct autogenerates them (fine); Repo.insert_all/3 would raise a not-null violation unless started_at/updated_at are supplied. TEST-DESIGNER should prefer Repo.insert! (or pass both timestamps to insert_all). Loud failure on first run, not a behavioural ambiguity.

MINOR (design section 6.3 / 9(e) wording, non-blocking): 'such an instance is committed before any subsequent delete/1 call ... reaches guard 3' and the @doc phrase 'delete afterwards for certainty' slightly overclaim: a create whose catalog read preceded the retire commit can in principle still be between R and P when a very quick follow-up delete runs guard 3 (the same narrow window, now limited to starts in flight at retire time). The design itself concedes the concurrent-with-retire case. ELIXIR-DEV should word the @doc as 'closes the window for every start that begins after the retire commits; only a start already in flight at retire time can still slip through', not 'certainty'.
Pre-existing/out of scope, already named by the design: update_scope/2 has the same blind spot (section 12); shared-DB 42P01 hazard requires MIX_TEST_PARTITION for committed-row tests.
Unchanged from round 1 and still true: nothing in lib/ or test/ was edited by this validation; nothing committed.
